_readme: Source for the Find the Herd demo routes. Answers are NOT in this file or anywhere in the repository — only salted SHA-256 hashes (answer_hashes). Run `node scripts/build-hunt.mjs` after editing; see docs/FIND_THE_HERD.md. Every coordinate, access note and on-site detail is unverified and flagged needs_onsite_check until someone walks the route.

checkpoints.name: Norlin Library
checkpoints.spot: Quadrangle side, below the west steps
checkpoints.access_note: Unverified: the Quad walks are paved and close to level. The west terrace is up a flight of steps; the check-in area is meant to include the walk below them so nobody has to climb.
checkpoints.entrance_note: Outdoors only. No need to go inside the library.
checkpoints.source: Hand-placed from the repository's walkway data (Norlin Library front walk) and the OpenStreetMap building centre in buildings.json.

checkpoints.name: Macky Auditorium
checkpoints.access_note: Unverified: approach from the Quad side. Check for a step-free route onto the plaza and whether events block it.
checkpoints.entrance_note: Outdoors only. Stay on the plaza; do not enter during rehearsals or performances.
checkpoints.source: Offset south of the OpenStreetMap building centre in buildings.json (MCKY).

checkpoints.name: Old Main
checkpoints.spot: Outside, by the plaque and bell
checkpoints.access_note: Unverified: paved walks from the Quad. Confirm where the plaque and bell actually are and move the pin there.
checkpoints.source: Offset east of the OpenStreetMap building centre in buildings.json (MAIN).

checkpoints.name: Mary Rippon Outdoor Theatre
checkpoints.spot: Outside only: entrance and garden path
checkpoints.access_note: Unverified: the theatre sits in the Hellems courtyard, which reopened in 2026 after renovation. Walk the new paths and pick a spot that is step-free and clearly outside the seating area.
checkpoints.entrance_note: Stay outside the theatre. Never enter the seating area: classes, rehearsals and performances happen here. If something is on, keep your voices down and solve from the path.
checkpoints.source: Estimated from the published theatre location and the Hellems building centre in buildings.json (HLMS). Least certain pin of the five.

checkpoints.name: University Memorial Center
checkpoints.access_note: Unverified: the South Terrace and the fountain court are on different sides of the building. This demo circle is centred on the building and wide enough to cover both. Choose one spot on site, then tighten the radius.
checkpoints.entrance_note: Outdoors only. The terrace is sometimes tented or reserved for events; use the fountain court if so.

editions.title: Demo Route — Edition 1
editions.intro: Look up, look closely. Every answer is something you can see from where you stand.

puzzles.prompt: Stand on the Quad side and look above the west doors. A sentence is carved in the stone. What is its last word?
hints: The sentence begins “Who knows only his own generation…”
Five letters. It’s what the sentence says you remain.
puzzles.onsite_note: Inscription is documented by CU Libraries. Confirm it is readable from the walk below the steps.

puzzles.prompt: Face Macky from the south plaza. How many tall towers rise above the front of the building?
hints: Count only the towers that stand above the roofline.
They frame the main entrance, one on each side.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm the number a student would count from the plaza and that the towers are visible from the pin. Change the answer in the admin view if it differs.

puzzles.prompt: Most of campus shares one look: rough stone walls under red tile roofs. Old Main came first and looks different. What are its walls made of?
hints: Small, rectangular, and baked rather than quarried.
Five letters, starting with B.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm wording works when standing by the plaque and bell.

puzzles.prompt: Stay on the path outside the theatre. The seating tiers are built from a local pink stone. Which kind of stone?
hints: It’s the same stone as the walls of most CU buildings.
The first half of the word is what beaches are made of.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm the seating can be seen from outside after the 2026 renovation. If not, swap this for a detail visible from the path.

puzzles.prompt: Find the fountain court beside the UMC. It is named for a screenwriter who studied at CU. What is his last name?
hints: Look for a sign or plaque by the fountain.
His first name is Dalton.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm there is a sign or plaque naming the court that a player can find.

editions.title: Demo Route — Edition 2
editions.intro: Names, dates and carved words become codes. Bring a little arithmetic.

puzzles.prompt: Count the words carved above the west doors. Multiply that by the number of letters in the last word.
hints: The sentence is ten words long.
The last word is CHILD.
puzzles.onsite_note: Uses the west-door inscription. Confirm it is readable from the check-in spot.

puzzles.prompt: Take the five letters of MACKY from the building’s name. Shift each one forward one place in the alphabet (A becomes B, B becomes C…). What do you get?
hints: M becomes N. Keep going.
The last letter, Y, becomes Z.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm the name MACKY appears on the building or a sign near the plaza.

puzzles.prompt: Old Main opened the same year Colorado became a state. Find that year here, then add its four digits together.
hints: Colorado is the Centennial State: it joined the Union 100 years after 1776.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm the year appears on the plaque or building. If it doesn’t, keep the puzzle (the hint covers it) or reword.

puzzles.prompt: The theatre is named for Mary Rippon, CU’s first woman professor. Take her last name, remove both copies of the letter that appears twice, and read what’s left backwards.
hints: The doubled letter is P.
R, I, O, N — now backwards.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm her name is on a sign visible from outside.

puzzles.prompt: Turn the letters U, M and C into their places in the alphabet (A = 1 … Z = 26) and add them up.
hints: U is the 21st letter.
puzzles.onsite_note: No on-site detail needed beyond the building’s initials.

editions.title: Demo Route — Edition 3
editions.intro: Nobody holds the whole puzzle. Each phone gets a piece; pass them around or pool them to finish it. Playing alone? One tap puts every piece on your screen.

puzzles.prompt: Each of you holds part of the instructions. Put them together to build a four-letter code.
pieces: The code is four letters, all taken from the sentence carved above the west doors.
Letters 1 and 2: the first letters of the first two words.
Letter 3: the first letter of the longest word.
Letter 4: the first letter of the last word.
hints: The sentence: “Who knows only his own generation remains always a child.”
Who, Knows … Generation … Child.

puzzles.prompt: Follow the steps in order. Each of you has one.
pieces: Step 1: start with the number of letters in MACKY.
Step 2: multiply by the number of letters in AUDITORIUM.
Step 3: add the number of vowels in AUDITORIUM.
Step 4: the total is your answer.
hints: MACKY has 5 letters and AUDITORIUM has 10.
A-U-D-I-T-O-R-I-U-M has six vowels.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm the full name MACKY AUDITORIUM appears nearby.

puzzles.prompt: Follow the steps in order. Each of you has one.
pieces: Step 1: Old Main opened the year Colorado became a state. Take the last two digits of that year.
Step 2: swap those two digits.
Step 3: add the number of letters in MAIN.
Step 4: the total is your answer.
hints: The year is 1876.
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm the year appears on the plaque or building.

puzzles.prompt: Put the letters in order to spell a name you can find here.
pieces: Six letters. R comes first and I follows it.
The doubled letter sits in the middle.
The doubled letter is P.
N is last, with O just before it.
hints: It’s the last name of the person this theatre honors.
Mary ______
puzzles.onsite_note: Confirm her name is on a sign visible from outside.

puzzles.prompt: Each of you has a number or a rule. Combine them.
pieces: U is the 21st letter of the alphabet.
M is the 13th letter.
C is the 3rd letter.
Multiply the smallest number by the largest, then add the middle one.
puzzles.onsite_note: No on-site detail needed beyond the building’s initials.
